schema.format: selector-family/v2; omitted means v2; explicit old v1 rejects.
schema.ordinary: Single program fields can be top-level. Multiple independent recipes remain programs. Ten original recipes actually use parameters plus payment and the common call compiler.
schema.funding: Shared selector/signature/parameters/meta naming, domain funding. Callback/repayment belong to execution; current liquidity/fee/priority belong to funding. Old root params/identity/observation/callback fields reject.
schema.metadata: Meta is stripped before normalization, program/declaration fingerprints, candidate ownership and module contract hashes; metadata-only changes preserve encoded execution and Ready ownership. Required behavior is never moved into meta.
schema.identity: No protocol identity admission prerequisite in the new funding or credit schemas. Selector plus complete canonical ABI owns family; target/pool/bound parameters and token identity scope instances/offers.

funding.providerScope: Every source/offer binds family, instance, provider, declared liquidity holder, pool scope, asset and offer ID; selection reaches encoder/repayment. No first-offer fallback.
funding.capacity: ERC20 balanceOf(holder) capacity key is chain plus holder plus asset, excluding selector and logical pool. Multiple selectors/pools cannot multiply one real balance.
funding.currentState: Current-session refresh obtains declared capacity and fee under the current source. Missing fee reads remain unresolved. Fee cache cannot be reused across selected amounts.
funding.security: Callback selector, caller, argument prefix and exact child bytes authenticated; amount/fee/source/actor mismatches reject. The full borrow-children-repay final simulation and profit/conservation gates remain.
funding.preparation: Existing shared effective-input max-hops policy still bounds simulation preparation; no funding-specific fixed four-hop constant introduced.
funding.behaviorChange: Balancer prior zero-fee template now reads current dynamic fee and rounds upward for the chosen amount; changed/missing fee cannot silently fall back to zero.

credit.normalization: same selector + full ABI owns candidate, instance and route; metadata is not semantic

baseNonEntry.reason: Base action/trace registration only; no projected route, Exact quote or execution recipe existed.

mathEquivalence.comparison: New pure JSON integer models versus base-fdb math.ts in offline migration verifier only

credit.runtimeDependencies: Production credit compiler uses generic native binding/execution and existing generic credit risk semantics; no retired Fluid TS/root JSON loader. Pure discovery imports read-flow/risk types only.
credit.proofs: Ready verifies actual current-executor operation, positive newly returned position, exact collateral/debt returns and token effects, source and transaction origin. Risk quote requires current config/oracle/exchange prices plus issued debt proof. No ordinary startup-simulation exemption or ordinary RuntimeLeg is advertised.
credit.policyIdentity: Credit and pricing policy semantic hash is compiler-owned program data; changing risk policy invalidates the candidate. Meta-only changes do not.
credit.historicalHarness: Fixture label may remain provenance, but selected credit family comes from observed selector/ABI and issued Ready routes. Full credit graph, domain and target checked; dedicated credit risk quote path preserved.

checkLimitations: This report records the listed implementation and local checks. Whole-repository builds, the final generated catalog and cross-family integration results are recorded separately in the delivery evidence.

No external archive/current-chain RPC, historical mainnet fork, mainnet broadcast or production profitability verdict is asserted here. Local fixtures and local EVM demonstrate contracts, not live protocol compatibility at an untested state.
area: Funding, original declarative migration and Fluid credit

basis: The supplied transaction observation is checked against candidate target, transaction hash and original source before selecting a catalog pattern.
Selection rebuilds every matching program candidate and requires both the candidate key and every decoder-owned field to match exactly; zero or multiple complete matches reject.

onlyPatternId is allowed only with an explicit family and supplied observation. Strict attestation selects exactly that catalog pattern and then runs the complete current-source lifecycle; a foreign pattern cannot fall back to the first recipe.
Reanchoring preserves the original evidence source while the current-source lifecycle checks the execution source. The selected recipe is not replaced after reanchoring.

The current change leaves the existing subset/resume runner and checkpoint code unchanged: candidate membership/hash, retained candidate accounting, parent/scope binding, source-plan resume checks, canonical fences and complete graph validation remain present.
